notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents, covering 2026-10-04 through 2026-10-06. All lanes hit routine EGRESS_BLOCKED on most org-domain WebFetch attempts and worked from WebSearch snippets instead, except platform.claude.com/docs, which was fetchable directly this run (worth other lanes trying it first in future runs rather than assuming it's blocked). Security lane ran 33+ queries and found zero new, sourceable items for the Oct 4-6 window — confirmed as a genuinely quiet day rather than a search failure, though WebSearch's index appears to lag real-time for CISA KEV bulletins by several days regardless of query phrasing. Bigtech/hardware/mobile lane flagged a real risk this cycle: several WebSearch AI-summaries blended in stale/mis-dated content from earlier years (an AMD event description that was actually 2024 coverage, a China chip-export result quoting a pre-2026 official, a Pixel 11 Pro Fold 'ships October 2026' claim contradicted by its actual August 2026 ship date already on the calendar) — all were cross-checked and dropped rather than filed. Devtools/cloud lane hit similar contradictory AI-summary issues on Kubernetes/Rust version-date pairings and dropped those too, filing only items corroborated by a real source URL. AI lane discarded an unsourced claim that Anthropic made 'the most powerful version of Claude' public on Oct 6, 2026 — could not corroborate against any primary source or named outlet, looks like a search-summarization artifact.
concerns: Confirmed via --dry-run (not just suspected) that src/lib/id.ts's token-overlap dedupe (isSameThing, 0.6 Jaccard floor) actively destroys data on sequential-version titles, not just risks it. Genuinely new, well-sourced findings this run — GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18 EOL (Oct 14 2026, docs.github.com/.../enterprise-server@3.18/admin/all-releases) and 3.19 EOL (Dec 9 2026, .../enterprise-server@3.19/admin/all-releases) — both fuzzy-matched onto the single existing 3.17 entry (6/8 = 0.75 token overlap, differing only in the version-number token and within the 75-day event-drift window), which would have let one silently overwrite the other and lose data. Far worse: five new Claude model-lifecycle findings (Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 — all titled '<Model> reaches minimum guaranteed support floor', sourced to Anthropic's own platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations, which was directly fetchable this run) cascaded: each one's title overlaps the existing 'Claude Opus 4.6 reaches minimum guaranteed support floor' entry by 7-8 of 9-10 tokens, so --dry-run showed all five sequentially matching and silently overwriting the SAME single 2027-02 Opus-4.6 entry, mutating its title each time, which would have collapsed six distinct real-world facts (4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 5, 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 retirement dates) into one entry retaining only the last-applied content. Dropped both the GHES 3.18/3.19 and all five Claude model-floor findings from this run rather than risk the overwrite — this is not a one-off, it is the same token-overlap floor being too permissive for any title family that differs only by a version number, and it will keep destroying data every time a run tries to file the next version in a sequence (model deprecation floors, server EOLs, SDK versions, etc.). This is urgent: a maintainer should special-case version-number tokens in isSameThing (require exact match on any token matching /^\d+(\.\d+)*$/ before considering two titles the same) so routine runs can file these without hand-dropping legitimate, well-sourced entries every day.

Two devtools/cloud candidates (Google Kubernetes Engine 1.35 EOL, and both GitHub Actions/Azure Pipelines runner-image removal dates for macOS 14 and Ubuntu 22.04) are sourced only to endoflife.ai/endoflife.date, a third-party aggregator — no search result surfaced a direct quote from cloud.google.com or github.blog for these specific dates, so they're filed at 'expected' rather than 'confirmed'. Worth a direct check against the primary pages if fetch access ever opens up.

Upgraded the existing 'Apple expected to require '27 SDKs for App Store Connect submissions' entry (data/events/2027-04.json, was confidence: expected) to confirmed — a MacObserver piece cites Apple's own developer.apple.com/news/ post (dated Sept 9, 2026) stating the April 2027 SDK requirement directly. Had to reuse the existing title verbatim to force the merge: a reworded title ('Apple requires ...' instead of 'Apple expected to require ...') tested at only 0.5 token-overlap against the original and would have created a duplicate row instead of correcting it — the mismatch traces to slugify()'s hard 60-character cap inside titleTokens(), which truncates 'submissions' to 'subm' on the longer existing title but leaves it whole on a shorter rephrasing, so two titles describing the same thing can land on opposite sides of the 0.6 floor purely based on length. Same standing id.ts fragility as the version-number collision noted above, different trigger.

An EU Cyber Resilience Act full-compliance deadline (CE marking, SBOM, secure-by-design obligations) lands December 11, 2027 per consistent secondary-source citation (mend.io, keyfactor.com, underdefense.com) — outside the current 12-month window from today, so not filed, but flagging now since it's a significant compliance cutover worth picking up once the window reaches it (the CRA's earlier Sept 11, 2026 reporting-goes-live milestone is already filed in 2026-09.json).
